mainTopic: אתנן of a זונה גויה according to אביי, and when brothers owe קלבון or מעשר בהמה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of a ברייתא about an אתנן animal that still enters the pen for מעשר בהמה. The ברייתא is set with a זונה גויה, because a non-Jew does not tithe and because payment to a Jewish זונה is not אתנן at all. This matches אביי's rule, learned through a גזירה שוה of תועבה from עריות: only a woman with whom קידושין cannot take effect makes her payment אתנן. אביי adds that a כהן gets no מלקות for לא יחלל זרעו with a גויה, since her child is not his זרע. A new משנה then teaches that brothers and partners owe either קלבון or מעשר בהמה, depending on whether they still hold their father's undivided estate or divided it and later rejoined. The גמרא learns the exemption of partners from מעשר בהמה from 'יהיה לך', using the method of אם אינו ענין. רבי ירמיה lists four combinations of the two laws, depending on whether the money or the animals were divided. Finally, אמוראים argue about what kind of division turns brothers into partners: רב ענן and רבי אלעזר say only a split that works like a trade does, while רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן say any split does.

steps.title: Why not let her tithe it herself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the explanation of the ברייתא: if the calf is not אתנן, the זונה should be able to tithe it herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let her tithe it herself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on how the ברייתא was just explained. If the unborn calf was never אתנן, why does the man need to buy it back for it to be tithed? The זונה could tithe it herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the earlier explanation, the calf was still inside its mother when it was given, so it never got the status of אתנן. If so, the calf is a normal animal that belongs to the זונה. She should be able to bring it into her own pen for מעשר בהמה, with no need for the man to buy it back.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment given to a זונה, which may not be brought as a קרבן
The tithe of animals: every tenth animal leaving the pen is holy

phrases.english: But let her tithe it herself!
phrases.notes: The man supposedly had to buy the animal back. Why not let the זונה do the tithing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier explanation of the ברייתא, given before this amud begins
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the man must buy the animal back from the זונה before it is tithed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the calf is not אתנן, it is a normal animal that belongs to her. She could tithe it herself, so buying it back would be unnecessary.

steps.title: The case is a non-Jewish זונה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a זונה גויה, and a non-Jew does not separate מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The ברייתא is speaking] about a gentile prostitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the זונה in the ברייתא is not Jewish. A non-Jew cannot do מעשר בהמה, so the man has to buy the calf back for it to be tithed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר בהמה is a מצוה only for Jews. If the animal stays with a non-Jewish woman, it will never be tithed. That is why the ברייתא needs the Jewish man to buy it back and bring it into his own pen.

phrases.english: With a gentile prostitute.
phrases.notes: Since she is a non-Jew, she is not obligated in מעשר בהמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The זונה could tithe the calf herself, so buying it back makes no sense
steps.terutzMaskana: She is a non-Jew who cannot tithe, so the man must buy the calf back

steps.title: Why not set the case with a Jewish זונה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא didn't describe a Jewish זונה who tithes the animal herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it set [the case] with a Jewish prostitute, and let her tithe it herself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. Why choose a non-Jewish זונה? The ברייתא could have described a Jewish זונה, who can tithe the animal herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Choosing a non-Jewish זונה forces an extra step, buying the animal back. A simpler setup would be a Jewish זונה who tithes it herself. The גמרא wants to know why the ברייתא chose the more complicated case.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it be set up (explained) as

phrases.english: But let it set [the case] with a Jewish prostitute,
and let her tithe it herself!
phrases.notes: The same words appear in step 1, but here they serve a new challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to set the ברייתא with a זונה גויה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Jewish זונה could tithe the animal herself, which would be a simpler case. So why did the ברייתא choose a non-Jew?

steps.title: Payment to a Jewish זונה is not אתנן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא chose a non-Jewish זונה in order to teach that payment to a Jewish זונה is not אתנן at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us that [payment to] a Jewish prostitute is not אתנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the choice of a non-Jewish זונה was on purpose. With a Jewish זונה there would be no אתנן problem at all, so the ברייתא is quietly teaching that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case were about a Jewish זונה, the animal would never have been אתנן in the first place. The whole discussion would have nothing to talk about. By setting the case with a non-Jew, the ברייתא shows that only payment to a non-Jewish זונה counts as אתנן.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up two different laws. Payment to a Jewish זונה is not אתנן, so the animal may be brought as a קרבן. But being with a Jewish זונה is still forbidden in other ways, as אביי shows next for a כהן.

phrases.english: It teaches us
that [payment to] a Jewish prostitute is not אתנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּזוֹנָה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית לָא הָוֵי אֶתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: The case was chosen on purpose to teach a rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A Jewish זונה would have been the simpler case to use
steps.terutzMaskana: A Jewish זונה's payment is not אתנן, so only a non-Jewish זונה makes sense in this ברייתא

steps.title: אביי's two-sided rule about non-Jewish and Jewish זונות
steps.stepSummary: This matches אביי. For a זונה גויה, her payment is forbidden, but a כהן is not given מלקות. For a זונה ישראלית, her payment is permitted, but a כהן is given מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like אביי, for אביי said: A gentile prostitute — her payment is forbidden, and a כהן who has relations with her is not flogged because of 'He shall not profane his seed.' A Jewish prostitute — her payment is permitted, and a כהן who has relations with her is flogged because of 'He shall not profane his seed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer with a statement of אביי. אביי says payment to a non-Jewish זונה is אתנן, while payment to a Jewish זונה is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's rule works in opposite directions. For a non-Jewish זונה, the payment is forbidden as אתנן, but a כהן who is with her does not get מלקות for לא יחלל זרעו, since her children are not considered his זרע. For a Jewish זונה, the payment is permitted, but the כהן does get מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: "He shall not profane his seed" (ויקרא כא:טו), a prohibition for a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: זונה גויה: her payment is אתנן (forbidden for a קרבן), but there are no מלקות for a כהן. זונה ישראלית: her payment is not אתנן (permitted), but a כהן does get מלקות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the law of אתנן and the כהן's prohibition of לא יחלל זרעו are separate laws. Each one depends on different factors.

phrases.english: In accordance with Abaye, for Abaye said:
A gentile prostitute — her payment is forbidden,
and a priest who has relations with her
is not flogged because of "He shall not profane his seed."
A Jewish prostitute — her payment is permitted,
and a priest who has relations with her
is flogged because of "He shall not profane his seed."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an אמורא's ruling that supports the answer in step 4
steps.raayaObject: That payment to a Jewish זונה is not אתנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's statement comparing a זונה גויה with a זונה ישראלית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment to a זונה גויה is אתנן and forbidden; payment to a זונה ישראלית is permitted. מלקות for a כהן under לא יחלל זרעו apply only with a Jewish זונה.

steps.title: Source: תועבה here, like תועבה in עריות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that אביי learns אתנן of a זונה גויה from a גזירה שוה: the word תועבה appears both by אתנן and by עריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A gentile prostitute — her payment is forbidden: he derives 'abomination' 'abomination' from the forbidden relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining where אביי gets his rule. He learns it from the word תועבה, which appears both in the פסוק about אתנן and in the פסוקים about עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about אתנן (דברים כג:יט) uses the word תועבה, and so does the section on עריות (ויקרא יח:כט). Through this גזירה שוה, אתנן is understood like עריות. In both, the relationship is one where קידושין cannot take effect, which fits a non-Jewish woman and not an unmarried Jewish woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Abomination; the key word linking the two sections
A teaching method that learns one law from another through a shared word

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that only a זונה גויה's payment is אתנן comes from a גזירה שוה: תועבה by אתנן, and תועבה by עריות.

phrases.english: A gentile prostitute — her payment is forbidden:
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the first part of אביי's rule in order to give its source.

phrases.english: he derives "abomination" "abomination" from the forbidden relations.
phrases.notes: תועבה appears in דברים כג:יט about אתנן, and in ויקרא יח:כט about עריות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the first part of אביי's rule from step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אתנן of a זונה גויה is forbidden, learned through a גזירה שוה of תועבה from עריות

steps.title: The גזירה שוה shows the זונה is one with whom קידושין cannot take effect
steps.stepSummary: Just as עריות are women with whom קידושין cannot take effect, the זונה of אתנן is also a woman with whom קידושין cannot take effect: a גויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as עריות are women with whom קידושין does not take effect, so too the זונה in the פסוק of אתנן is a woman with whom קידושין does not take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the גזירה שוה from Step 6. It spells out exactly what we learn from comparing אתנן to עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With most עריות, a man's קידושין does not take effect at all. The shared word תועבה teaches that the זונה of אתנן must be the same kind of woman. A Jewish woman can receive קידושין, so this must mean a גויה, since קידושין never takes effect with her.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden relationships listed in the תורה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for אביי's rule that only a זונה גויה's payment is forbidden as אתנן. That explains why a Jewish זונה's payment is permitted.

phrases.english: Just as forbidden relations,
with whom betrothal does not take effect,
so too the prostitute is that one
with whom betrothal does not take effect.
phrases.notes: This means a gentile woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה עֲרָיוֹת, דְּלָא תָּפְסִי בְּהוּ קִדּוּשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the גזירה שוה that was introduced in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זונה of אתנן is a woman with whom קידושין cannot take effect, meaning a גויה.

steps.title: Why a כהן is not given מלקות for a זונה גויה
steps.stepSummary: A כהן who lives with a זונה גויה is not given מלקות for 'לא יחלל זרעו', because her children are not considered his seed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן who lives with her is not given מלקות because of 'he shall not profane his seed.' The תורה said he must not profane his seed, and this child is not his seed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the second half of אביי's ruling from Step 5: why a כהן is not given מלקות for a זונה גויה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition is worded as not profaning 'his seed,' meaning his children. A child born to a non-Jewish mother is a non-Jew. Halachically, that child is not counted as the כהן's descendant at all. So the reason behind this מלקות never applies here.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not profane his seed (children)
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי: a זונה גויה's payment is אתנן, but a כהן gets no מלקות with her. A זונה ישראלית's payment is not אתנן, but a כהן does get מלקות with her.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not make it permitted for a כהן to be with a גויה. It only means he is not given מלקות under 'לא יחלל זרעו'.

phrases.english: And a priest who has relations with her
is not flogged
because of 'he shall not profane his seed,'
for the Merciful One said 'he shall not profane his seed,'
and this one is not his seed.
phrases.notes: A child of a non-Jewish mother is not counted as his descendant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of אביי's ruling, now that the first half has been sourced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are no מלקות for 'לא יחלל זרעו' with a זונה גויה, because her children are not his seed.

steps.title: New משנה: brothers and partners owe either קלבון or מעשר בהמה
steps.stepSummary: Brothers and partners who are obligated in קלבון are exempt from מעשר בהמה. Those obligated in מעשר בהמה are exempt from קלבון.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Brothers and partners who must pay קלבון are exempt from מעשר בהמה. Those who must give מעשר בהמה are exempt from קלבון.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that brothers or partners fall into one of two groups: they owe קלבון or they owe מעשר בהמה, never both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קלבון is a small extra fee added when people pay the half-shekel together, so it applies when they are treated as separate partners. מעשר בהמה does not apply to animals owned in a partnership. It does apply when the brothers are treated like one household still running their father's estate. Each status brings one obligation and removes the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A small premium added to the half-shekel payment
Tithe of animals: every tenth animal is sanctified

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one ownership status decides two separate הלכות in opposite directions.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Brothers and partners,
when they are obligated in the premium,
they are exempt from animal tithe;
when they are obligated in animal tithe,
they are exempt from the premium.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, unrelated to the אתנן discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Obligation in קלבון and obligation in מעשר בהמה exclude each other for brothers and partners.

steps.title: When brothers are obligated in מעשר בהמה and when in קלבון
steps.stepSummary: Brothers who acquired animals from their father's undivided estate are obligated in מעשר בהמה. If they divided the estate and then rejoined, they owe קלבון and are exempt from מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they acquired the animals from the father's estate, they are obligated in מעשר בהמה. If not, they are exempt. If they divided the estate and then became partners again, they owe קלבון and are exempt from מעשר בהמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now explains which brothers belong in which group from Step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals still held from the undivided estate count as one household's property, so מעשר בהמה applies. Once the brothers divide, each becomes a separate owner. Their new joint ownership is a partnership, which is exempt from מעשר בהמה but triggers קלבון.

keyTerms.meaning: The father's estate, still held as one undivided unit

steps.whatToRemember: Undivided inheritance means מעשר בהמה, not קלבון. Divided and then rejoined means קלבון, not מעשר בהמה.

phrases.english: If they acquired from the estate of the house, they are obligated;
and if not, they are exempt.
If they divided, then went back and became partners,
they are obligated in the premium
and exempt from animal tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the cases that fall under the general rule of Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An undivided inheritance is obligated in מעשר בהמה. A partnership formed after division owes קלבון and is exempt from מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: A ברייתא learns that partners are exempt from מעשר בהמה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'יהיה לך' that animals owned by partners are exempt from מעשר בהמה. The extra word 'יהיה' includes brothers who own animals from their father's undivided estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'Shall be yours' means only what belongs to you, and not what belongs to partners. One might think this applies even when brothers acquired animals from their father's undivided estate. Therefore the verse says 'shall be' to include them in the obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that gives the פסוק source for the משנה's rule. Partners are exempt from מעשר בהמה, but heirs of an undivided estate are obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לך' (yours) points to one owner, so partners are excluded. The word 'יהיה' then brings back one special group: brothers who have not yet divided their father's estate. The estate is still treated as one 'house', so it does not count as a partnership.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught; this introduces a ברייתא
The holdings of the father's house, an inherited estate that has not been divided

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the פסוק basis for the משנה's rule that brothers in an undivided estate are obligated in מעשר בהמה, while true partners are exempt.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
'Shall be yours' means it must be yours, and not owned by partners.
One might think this applies even if they acquired the animals through the undivided holdings of the father's house?
phrases.notes: This means brothers who inherited and have not yet divided the estate.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: 'Shall be.'
phrases.notes: The extra word includes heirs who have not divided the estate.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״יִהְיֶה לְךָ״ — וְלֹא שֶׁל שׁוּתָּפוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the משנה's rules about brothers and partners that were summarized in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Partners are exempt from מעשר בהמה ('לך'), but heirs of an undivided estate are obligated ('יהיה').

steps.title: But that verse is about בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the verse 'יהיה לך' is written about בכור, not about מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this verse is written about the firstborn animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's source. The verse it used is about בכור, so how can it teach a rule about מעשר בהמה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא took a rule about מעשר בהמה from a פסוק whose context is clearly בכור. The objection attacks the link between the verse and the law, not the law itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn animal, which is holy and given to the כהן

phrases.english: But this verse is written regarding the firstborn!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'יהיה לך' as a source for מעשר בהמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse's context is בכור, so it should not teach a law about מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: Since partners are obligated in בכור, the verse is applied to מעשר בהמה
steps.stepSummary: Another פסוק, 'ובכורות בקרכם וצאנכם', shows that partners are obligated in בכור. So 'יהיה לך' cannot be excluding partners from בכור, and it is transferred to מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the verse is not needed for בכור, since בכור applies even to partners, as it is written 'and the firstborn of your herds and your flocks', then apply it to מעשר בהמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with the method of 'אם אינו ענין'. A verse that cannot teach anything in its own topic is moved to a related topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural 'your herds' (בקרכם) shows that בכור applies even to jointly owned animals. If 'יהיה לך' excluded partners from בכור, it would contradict that verse. So the exclusion is applied to מעשר בהמה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for its own topic, a rule for moving a verse's teaching to another topic
Apply it to the topic of
Your herds and your flocks, in plural form, which includes partners
Animal tithe, where every tenth animal is made holy

steps.confusionAlert: The verse is not saying that partners are exempt from בכור. They are obligated in בכור. The exemption for partners is only for מעשר בהמה.

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the matter of the firstborn,
since the firstborn obligation does apply in a partnership,
as it is written: 'And the firstborn of your herds and your flocks' (plural),
apply it to the matter of animal tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the verse to another topic (אם אינו ענין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse is about בכור, so it cannot teach about מעשר בהמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Partners are obligated in בכור from another פסוק, so the exclusion in 'יהיה לך' is applied to מעשר בהמה.
steps.whatToRemember: Partners are obligated in בכור but exempt from מעשר בהמה. The source is 'יהיה לך', moved to מעשר בהמה through 'אם אינו ענין'.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה lists four combinations of קלבון and מעשר בהמה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says there are four possibilities: obligated in both, exempt from both, obligated only in קלבון, or obligated only in מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Sometimes they are obligated in both. Sometimes they are exempt from both. Sometimes they are obligated in קלבון and exempt from מעשר בהמה. And sometimes they are obligated in מעשר בהמה and exempt from קלבון.
steps.whatsHappening: Returning to the משנה about brothers and partners, רבי ירמיה gives a list of four outcomes. This step sets up the next lines, which explain each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made it sound like the two laws always go opposite ways: partners pay קלבון but are exempt from מעשר בהמה. רבי ירמיה adds that, depending on what the brothers divided, both laws can apply together, or neither can apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A small extra fee added when paying the half-שקל, for example when two people pay one coin together

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
There are times they are obligated in this and in that,
and times they are exempt from this and from that,

phrases.aramaic: פְּעָמִים שֶׁחַיָּיבִין בַּקָּלְבּוֹן וּפְטוּרִין מִמַּעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה,
phrases.english: times they are obligated in the premium and exempt from animal tithe,

phrases.aramaic: וּפְעָמִים שֶׁחַיָּיבִין בְּמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה וּפְטוּרִין מִן הַקָּלְבּוֹן.
phrases.english: and times they are obligated in animal tithe and exempt from the premium.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: פְּעָמִים שֶׁחַיָּיבִין בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's rules about קלבון and מעשר בהמה (steps 9-10) and expands them into four cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Obligation in קלבון and in מעשר בהמה can appear in all four combinations.

steps.title: Obligated in both: they divided the money but not the animals
steps.stepSummary: The brothers are obligated in both laws when they divided the inherited money but left the animals undivided.
steps.simpleTranslation: Obligated in both: when they divided the money but did not divide the animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining רבי ירמיה's list, starting with the case where both obligations apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animals were not divided, so they are still the father's estate, and מעשר בהמה applies. The money was divided, so for the half-שקל they count as separate people, and when they pay together they owe קלבון, like partners.

keyTerms.meaning: Money, here the money inherited from the father

phrases.english: Obligated in this and in that —
when they divided the money but did not divide the animals,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first case in רבי ירמיה's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When are the brothers obligated in both?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the money was divided but the animals were not.

steps.title: Exempt from both: they divided the animals but not the money
steps.stepSummary: The brothers are exempt from both laws when they divided the animals but left the money undivided.
steps.simpleTranslation: Exempt from both: when they divided the animals but did not divide the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second case in the list, where neither obligation applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of the previous case. The animals were divided, so if they are held together, they are owned by partners, and partners are exempt from מעשר בהמה. The money is still the father's undivided estate, so paying the half-שקל from it does not create קלבון.
steps.confusionAlert: Be careful not to mix up which item makes which law apply. The status of the animals decides מעשר בהמה. The status of the money decides קלבון.

phrases.english: Exempt from this and from that —
when they divided the animals but did not divide the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second case in רבי ירמיה's list, as the mirror image of step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When are the brothers exempt from both?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the animals were divided but the money was not.

steps.title: Obligated in the premium but exempt from animal tithe
steps.stepSummary: Third case of רבי ירמיה: the brothers divided both the money and the animals and then joined again. They owe the קלבון but are exempt from מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are obligated in the קלבון and exempt from מעשר בהמה when they divided both this and that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third of רבי ירמיה's four cases. The brothers split everything, both the money and the animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the brothers have divided everything, the father's estate no longer exists. If they then join together again, they are ordinary partners, like two strangers. Ordinary partners who give one coin for both of them owe the קלבון, and animals owned by partners are exempt from מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: A small extra fee added when paying the half-shekel, for example when one coin is given for two people
The tithe of animals: every tenth newborn animal is set aside
Partners; their shared animals are exempt from מעשר בהמה
They divided the inheritance between them

phrases.english: They are obligated in the premium
phrases.notes: The extra fee paid when two people give one shekel together.

phrases.english: and exempt from the animal tithe —
when they divided both this and that.
phrases.notes: "This and that" means the money and the animals. Afterward they became partners again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list from steps 15 and 16 by defining the third possibility.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When both the money and the animals were divided, the brothers are ordinary partners: they owe the קלבון and are exempt from מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: Obligated in animal tithe but exempt from the premium
steps.stepSummary: Fourth case of רבי ירמיה: the brothers divided nothing. They owe מעשר בהמה but are exempt from the קלבון.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are obligated in מעשר בהמה and exempt from the קלבון when they did not divide either this or that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last of the four cases. The brothers never split anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When nothing has been divided, the whole estate still counts as the father's single property. The father's money is treated as paying the shekel, so there is no premium. Because the flock has a single owner, מעשר בהמה applies.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not divide; the inheritance is still one undivided estate

steps.whatToRemember: The money decides the קלבון: undivided money means no premium, divided money means premium. The animals decide מעשר בהמה: undivided animals mean tithe, divided animals mean exemption.

phrases.english: They are obligated in the animal tithe
and exempt from the premium —
when they did not divide either this or that.
phrases.notes: The estate stays as if the father still owns it.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּיבִין בְּמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה וּפְטוּרִין מִן הַקָּלְבּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the four-case list that רבי ירמיה began.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When nothing was divided, the brothers owe מעשר בהמה and are exempt from the קלבון.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new idea רבי ירמיה is teaching, since all four cases seem to follow simply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ירמיה: his four cases seem too simple to need saying. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case seems to follow directly from one rule: divided money means premium, and divided animals mean no tithe. If so, the list adds nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: "It's obvious!" The גמרא asks why a statement needed to be said at all

phrases.english: Isn't it obvious?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the four-case list that was just completed teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every case follows straightforwardly from the basic rules, so the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Dividing the animals does not show they divided the money
steps.stepSummary: The case that needed teaching is where the animals were divided but the money was not. We might have thought dividing the animals shows the brothers intend to divide everything, so they would owe the קלבון. רבי ירמיה teaches that they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case where they divided the animals but not the money was needed. You might have thought: since they divided the animals, they have shown that they plan to divide everything, so they should owe the קלבון. He teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that one case, from step 16, really was a new teaching. Dividing the animals does not make the money count as divided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this teaching, we might say the brothers' intention to split everything is enough to treat the money as divided as well. רבי ירמיה shows that only actual division of the money counts. Until the money is split, the father's estate still pays the shekel, so there is no קלבון.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed for him; this part of the statement is a real new teaching
"It might have entered your mind to say": the mistaken first thought
"He teaches us": the actual new point

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that in these laws, actual division decides the status, not what the brothers plan to do.

phrases.english: Where they divided the animals but did not divide the money
was necessary for him to teach,
since it might enter your mind to say:
since they divided the animals,
they revealed their intent that they stand ready to divide everything,
so they should be obligated in the premium —
therefore he teaches us that they are not.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָלְקוּ בַּבְּהֵמָה וְלֹא חָלְקוּ בַּכְּסָפִים אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'isn't it obvious' challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the one case that is not obvious (צריכותא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dividing the animals shows the brothers plan to divide everything, so the money would count as divided and they would owe the קלבון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Intention does not count; until the money is actually divided, they are exempt from the קלבון.

steps.title: רב ענן limits the rule to splitting kids against goats
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן says the exemption from מעשר בהמה for brothers who divided and joined again applies only when they split the flock as kids for goats and goats for kids.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said: They taught this only where they divided kids against goats and goats against kids.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן adds a limit to the rule that divided brothers are treated like partners and exempt from מעשר בהמה. The exemption applies only to a certain kind of division.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each brother originally inherited a share of both the kids and the goats. If one takes all the goats and the other all the kids, each one has really traded his share of one kind for his brother's share of the other. That is like buying, so they become like strangers, and when they join again they are partners who are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: "They taught this only in a case of": a phrase that narrows a rule

steps.confusionAlert: רב ענן is not narrowing the קלבון rule. He is narrowing the exemption from מעשר בהמה for brothers who divided the animals.

phrases.english: Rav Anan said:
They taught this only
where they divided kids against goats
and goats against kids.
phrases.notes: One brother took all of one kind and the other took all of the other kind, which works like a trade.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עָנָן לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section that limits the משנה's rule (step 10) that brothers who divided and then rejoined are exempt from מעשר בהמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brothers who divided the animals are exempt from מעשר בהמה only if they split kids against goats, which works like a trade and makes them like buyers.

steps.title: An even division means each brother took his own share
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן finishes his statement. If the brothers split kids against kids and goats against goats, each one is seen as taking what was his from the start, so they are not exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they divided kids against kids and goats against goats, we say: this is the share that was coming to him from the very beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב ענן's statement from step 21 by giving the opposite case. When the brothers split the flock evenly, each one getting the same kinds of animals, the exemption does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting kids against goats is like a trade, since each brother gives up one kind of animal to get another. Splitting each kind evenly is not a trade, because each brother simply takes the part that was always his (an idea close to ברירה). So when they join again, they go back to being heirs of one estate, and heirs owe מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: The share that is coming to him
From the very first moment (from the start)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of split. 'Kids for goats' (step 21) is a trade, so they are exempt. 'Kids for kids, goats for goats' (this step) is not a trade, so they are obligated.

phrases.english: But if they divided kids against kids
and goats against goats
one says: this is his share
phrases.notes: Each brother's group of animals

phrases.english: that was coming to him from the start for this
phrases.notes: So no trade happened, and on rejoining they owe מעשר בהמה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רב ענן's statement, giving the contrasting case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An even split (kids for kids, goats for goats) is seen as each brother taking his original share, so after rejoining they are obligated in מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: רב נחמן says even an even split does not count as each taking his own share
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees with רב ענן. Even if they split kids for kids and goats for goats, we do not say each took his original share, so they are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: even if they divided kids against kids and goats against goats, we do not say that this is the share that was coming to him from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives an opposing view to רב ענן. For him, any division, even an even one, ends the brothers' status as heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן does not accept the idea that each brother's part was 'his from the start.' So every division counts as if they traded with each other. When they join again they are just partners, and partners are exempt from מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who argues here with רב ענן

steps.whyThisMatters: The disagreement depends on whether a division looks back and shows what each heir owned all along, a basic question that comes up in many סוגיות.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
Even if they divided kids against kids
and goats against goats
we do not say: this is his share
that was coming to him from the start for this
phrases.notes: So they are like partners and exempt

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רב ענן's limit in steps 21-22
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any division, even an even one, is not seen as each taking his original share, so brothers who rejoin are always exempt from מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר limits the exemption to an uneven split of nine against ten
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the exemption was taught only when they split nine big goats against ten kids.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: they only taught this when they divided nine against ten and ten against nine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אמורא, רבי אלעזר, who explains the same issue using numbers. This is the first half of his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nine big goats are worth about the same as ten kids. If one brother takes the nine big ones and the other takes the ten kids, that is really a trade. So when they rejoin they are like strangers who became partners, and they are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of
An אמורא who gives a view like רב ענן's

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
They taught this only
when they divided nine against ten
phrases.notes: Nine big goats for ten kids

phrases.english: and ten against nine
phrases.notes: A trade of similar value, so they are exempt

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second אמורא giving the same kind of limit as רב ענן, in numbers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brothers who divided and rejoined are exempt only when the split was a trade, such as nine big goats for ten kids.

steps.title: An even nine-for-nine and ten-for-ten split counts as each taking his own share
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר finishes. If they split nine against nine and ten against ten, each took his own original share, so they are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they divided nine against nine and ten against ten, we say: this is the share that was coming to him from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of רבי אלעזר's statement, giving the opposite case. When each brother takes the same numbers of each kind, it is not a trade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each brother got nine big goats and ten kids, so nobody gave up one kind of animal to get another. We say each just took what was always his, and on rejoining they are heirs again and owe מעשר בהמה. This matches רב ענן and goes against רב נחמן.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ענן and רבי אלעזר: a split that is a trade (kids for goats, nine for ten) means exempt, but an even split means each took his own share, so obligated. רב נחמן: any split means exempt.

phrases.english: But if they divided nine against nine
and ten against ten
one says: this is his share
that was coming to him from the start for this
phrases.notes: So on rejoining they owe מעשר בהמה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רבי אלעזר's statement, giving the contrasting case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An even split (nine for nine, ten for ten) is seen as each brother taking his original share, so after rejoining they are obligated in מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: Even an even split does not show original ownership
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן argues with רבי אלעזר. Even if the brothers split nine big goats against nine and ten kids against ten, we do not say each took his original share, so they are exempt from מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: even if they split nine against nine and ten against ten, we do not say that this is the share he was entitled to from the very start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite view to רבי אלעזר. Even when the brothers split the animals into perfectly matching groups, he says each brother is not seen as having owned his group from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said a matching split (same kind, same number) shows each brother simply took what was always his. Then they were never really buyers from each other, so they are obligated. רבי יוחנן rejects this: no matter how even the split is, we do not look back and say this share was his from the beginning (no ברירה). So the brothers count like buyers and then partners, and they are exempt from מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Against, matching (one group set against another)
His share that comes to him (that he is entitled to)
From the first moment, from the very start (from the father's death)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two pairs of opinions here. רב ענן and רבי אלעזר say a matching split means each brother took his own original share, so he is obligated. רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן say we never assume that (no ברירה), so the brothers count as partners and are exempt from מעשר בהמה.
steps.confusionAlert: The word "אפילו" ("even") is a clue. רבי יוחנן agrees with רבי אלעזר that an uneven split (nine goats against ten kids) is exempt. He disagrees only about the even split, and he says even that case is exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument is a practical use of the idea of ברירה. Can we decide now, looking back, that a share of an inheritance was always one person's? רבי יוחנן's view fits his well-known position that brothers who divide an inheritance are like buyers (האחין שחלקו לקוחות הן).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
phrases.notes: Brings an opposing view to רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: Even if they divided nine large goats for nine,
phrases.notes: This is exactly the case where רבי אלעזר said they are obligated.

phrases.english: and ten kids for ten,
phrases.notes: A perfectly matching split of each kind.

phrases.english: one does not say that this is his share
phrases.notes: We do not decide, looking back, that the share was his all along.

phrases.english: which came to him from the very start.
phrases.notes: So the brothers count as partners and are exempt from מעשר בהמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אלעזר (steps 24-25). It matches the way רב נחמן (step 23) disagreed with רב ענן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when the brothers split the animals evenly by kind and number, we do not treat each share as his from the start. So brothers who joined again are exempt from מעשר בהמה.
